post.caption: Schiaparelli's fur bracelet inspired a teacup. In 1936, artist Meret Oppenheim wore a bracelet covered in fur that she had designed for Schiaparelli's fashion house. At a Paris cafe, Picasso noticed it and joked that anything could wear fur. Oppenheim replied, even this cup and saucer, and covered a store bought set in fur. Surrealist leader Andre Breton named it Luncheon in Fur, nodding to Manet. At a New York show, visitors called it the quintessential Surrealist object. It was the first work by a woman that the Museum of Modern Art acquired.
